brief: Doctrine rewrite of 2026-08-21: every line is about the weather; the picture is the evidence. Three lines per photograph (Al’s ruled keeps locked and counted). Bank rescues marked. PAIRING-TASTE + the swap test still bind.
linesLabel: three per image incl. locked keeps

images.seen: Joburg highway gridlock under a massive purple storm, one lightning bolt over the skyline, wet lanes shining with brake lights. Monday.
lines: Lightning over the skyline and brake lights all the way in: Joburg is up early.
The slow lane, the fast lane, and the sky lane — only one is moving.
Somewhere a weather reporter is living their best life.

images.seen: A huge branched lightning strike over a modern estate street in rain, parked cars lit by the flash. Tuesday.
lines: That one landed close enough to count the seconds on one hand.
The whole street went daylight for a quarter of a second.
Every dog in the suburb filed a report at the same instant.

images.seen: Mammatus clouds glowing purple and pink over a windpomp and a sunflower field, orange horizon burning below. Wednesday.
lines: Those bubble clouds are the storm's signature, written on the way out.
That is the back page of a storm, and it reads better than the front.
The windpomp has seen a thousand of these and still stopped to look.

images.seen: A couple lying on the bedroom floor in soft morning light, coaxing a wide-eyed dachshund out from under the bed after the storm. Thursday.
lines: The storm passed an hour ago; the news has not reached under the bed yet.
The sky has moved on. The dachshund is requesting written confirmation.
The dog's under the bed. Smart move, honestly.

images.seen: Five shoppers sheltering under a mall's glass canopy at dusk, watching lightning strike beyond the wet parking lot, trolleys abandoned mid-row. Tuesday.
lines: The gap between flashes is being counted by everyone under this roof.
The trolleys are staying exactly where the storm interrupted them.
Five strangers, one roof, one unspoken agreement: not yet.

images.seen: A surfer in a wetsuit walking towards heavy storm surf under an enormous dark sky, board under his arm, rain already falling out at sea. Saturday.
lines: That sky would send most people home; it is sending him in.
The storm is doing the wave-making and he is doing the arithmetic.
Big sky, bigger sea, one board: the argument for staying home lost.

images.seen: A woman grimacing over a completely skeletonised umbrella in a wind-blasted street, leaves flying, palms bending, dark storm sky. Monday.
lines: The umbrella is now a diagram of an umbrella.
Leaves in the street, spokes in the air: the storm is winning on all fronts.
The wind has a personal vendetta against umbrellas.

images.seen: Two farmers in hats loading hay bales onto a bakkie in golden light, a dark storm wall already dumping rain on the mountains behind them. Thursday.
lines: That storm is twenty minutes out and both of them know the maths.
The sky set the deadline; the bakkie gets loaded to it.
The mountains are already getting theirs; this hay has about twenty minutes.

images.seen: A woman on a high apartment balcony watching lightning fork over the suburbs at a burning sunset, wet street and small umbrellas far below. Monday.
lines: The balcony beats the couch when the sky is doing this.
Sunset on one side, artillery on the other, and she has the balcony.
The storm is doing the rounds of the suburbs and saving town for last.

images.seen: A dark estate street at dusk, lightning glowing inside the cloud, palms bending in the wind, windows lit by candles. Wednesday.
lines: Candles in the windows: the storm has already had a word with the power.
The palms are pointing the way the storm is going, which is this way.
Lightning inside the cloud: the storm is still deciding where to put it.

images.seen: Two lightning bolts striking the sea beyond storm surf on a rocky coast, orange sunset squeezed under the purple cloud. Sunday.
lines: The sea is taking the strikes tonight so the land doesn't have to.
Sunset tried to happen; the storm had other bookings for that sky.
The waves were the show until the sky decided otherwise.

images.seen: A zinc bucket in the hallway catching a slow ceiling drip, folded towel beside it, the rainy garden visible through the open door. Friday.
lines: The roof has an opinion tonight and the bucket is taking minutes.
One drip, one bucket, one towel: the storm has made it indoors, barely.
Somewhere up there the rain found a way in, and it is being managed.

images.seen: A grinning man filming a giant lightning strike on his phone from the bedroom window, the suburb lit below. Sunday.
lines: Every South African storm gets filmed vertical, and this one earned it.
The strike lasted half a second; the video will last the whole group chat.
The sky does one take and expects you to be ready.

images.seen: A runner in black kit standing in the road with hands on hips, glaring up at a heavy grey storm sky before his run, stone house behind. Saturday.
lines: Warm-up done; now he is waiting on a ruling from upstairs.
The sky is loading something and the question is whether it lands mid-run.
Hands on hips: the international sign for arguing with weather.

images.seen: A woman in a gown with her coffee on the porch at dawn, watching twin pink lightning strikes over the mountains, wet street below. Sunday.
lines: The storm is keeping to the mountains, and the stoep is keeping the view.
First coffee of the day, best show of the week, same ten minutes.
The rain has been and gone; the electricity is still saying goodbye.

images.seen: A bakkie driving away down a red dirt road between mealie fields, dust glowing in the last light under an orange storm-lit horizon. Friday.
lines: That horizon is half sunset, half warning, and the bakkie knows the difference.
Dust now, mud by dark — that cloud bank is not decoration.
The mealies have been waiting for that cloud longer than anyone in the bakkie.

images.seen: Two golfers with their bags on the fairway, watching a lightning strike come down the course, trees whipping in the wind. Wednesday.
lines: The eighteenth can wait; the sky is playing through.
That is the course's way of saying the round is over.
Two club selections left: the clubhouse or the car.

images.seen: An empty rugby stadium under an enormous black storm cloud, lightning behind the stands, floodlights on, pitch shining wet. Saturday.
lines: Kickoff is under review by the only official that outranks the referee.
The floodlights are on; the sky brought its own anyway.
The pitch is ready, the lines are marked, and the weather has the whistle.

images.seen: Storm aftermath on a bushveld lawn — wicker chairs flipped, cushions scattered, a lounger on its side, branches down, trees still bending under a dark sky. Tuesday.
lines: The storm rearranged the stoep furniture and did not ask anybody first.
The chairs are down, the branches are down, and the sky is not done.
Every loose object in the garden has chosen violence.

images.seen: An old farmer at the door of his rusted corrugated shed, hand on his hat, watching a massive black storm and dust wall roll across the dry veld. Sunday.
lines: He has seen fifty of these arrive, and he still comes out to watch.
Dust first, rain second: the order of business is written on the horizon.
The drought and the storm are about to have a word, and he wants to hear it.

images.seen: A hadeda walking the dry verge of an empty Karoo-dorp street, white flat-roofed houses under an ominous dark storm sky. Monday.
lines: The street cleared out early; only the hadeda is finishing its rounds.
The sky is stacking up over the dorp and even the palm has gone still.
Even the hadedas are quiet.

images.seen: An emergency vehicle with its lights on in a wet estate street strewn with downed branches, storm clearing into sunset behind. Saturday.
lines: The storm made one pass and left the street a week of gardening.
Branches down, lights on, storm gone: the after-party is all admin.
The sunset is back like nothing happened; the trees know otherwise.

images.seen: A young man on a high balcony at dusk filming a double lightning strike over the city, rain beading on the glass railing. Tuesday.
lines: Two strikes in one frame: the sky is doing his content for him.
Rain on the railing, lightning on the horizon, phone doing its best.
That strike will look half this size on the phone, and he knows it.

images.seen: A boy wrapped in a fleece blanket at the bedroom window, watching a lightning bolt come down over the suburb at night. Wednesday.
lines: First storm he has stayed up for, and the sky is making it count.
Thunder is scary from bed and magnificent from a window; he moved.
The best television in the house is currently the weather.

images.seen: A couple laughing as they position a bucket to catch a ceiling leak directly over their bed, duvet already wet, storm-dark window behind. Saturday.
lines: The storm found the ceiling's weak spot; the bucket arrived three drops later.
The rain is now technically a house guest, and it chose the main bedroom.
Leak over the bed, laughter over the leak: married storm protocol.

images.seen: A farmer hauling a blue tarp over hay bales on a bakkie while hail comes down, storm-dark sky and a lit farmhouse behind him. Friday.
lines: Hail on the way down and a tarp halfway on: this one is going to be close.
The sky is throwing ice and he is answering with a tarp.
Hail gives you about ninety seconds of warning, and he is using all of them.

images.seen: A big dog with wide eyes lying flat under the dining table, lightning forking outside the patio doors behind the chairs. Friday.
lines: The spot under the table was chosen scientifically: furthest from the sky.
Thunder counts double when you have ears like that.
One flash outside and the seating plan changed itself.

images.seen: An abandoned club cricket pitch under a black-green storm sky — covers half-dragged on, kit and jerseys dumped on the grass, the sightscreen blown askew. Thursday.
lines: Bad light stopped play, then the light got a lot worse.
The covers made it on; the kit did not make it off.
A sky that colour clears a cricket field faster than any umpire.

images.seen: A white plastic chair overturned in a roadside puddle, a yellow farmhouse behind, columns of rain falling from the dark cloud on the horizon. Wednesday.
lines: The first casualty is a plastic chair, and the storm is not even here yet.
That rain on the horizon is about ten minutes from this puddle.
The wind came through first and signed its work with one white chair.

images.seen: A man wrestling the patio umbrella closed as a black storm front swallows the last of the sunshine, leaves flying across the tiles. Thursday.
lines: The umbrella is coming down in the storm's final two minutes of notice.
Half the sky is still summer; the other half is why he is hurrying.
Leaves already sideways: the storm sent its calling card ahead.

images.seen: A young man in a parked car filming a lightning bolt through the rain-beaded windscreen, wet suburban street beyond. Sunday.
lines: The car is the best hide this country makes for lightning season.
Rain on the glass, bolt in the frame, and not one drop on the photographer.
Front-row seats, full cover, wipers off: storm-watching done properly.

images.why: round-1 lines retired by the doctrine redo
images.seen: A night storm over a suburban street — rain slanting through the streetlight, lightning glowing behind the clouds, one big bare tree over the walls. Tuesday.
lines: The rain is coming through the streetlight at forty-five degrees, which means wind joined in.
Lightning behind the cloud: the storm is working with the lights off.
That old tree has stood through a hundred of these and is counting this one too.

images.why: round-1 lines retired by the doctrine redo
images.seen: Lightning splitting a purple night sky over a double garage, the gutter overflowing in a stream past the hosepipe, jacaranda petals on the wet paving. Monday.
lines: The gutter gave up on the downpipe and started its own waterfall.
Purple sky, purple petals: the storm colour-matched the driveway tonight.
The overflow says the roof got a month of rain in one evening.

images.why: round-1 lines retired by the doctrine redo
images.seen: An enclosed stoep at night with rain sheeting off the roof edge in a solid curtain past a strelitzia, one bulb burning, wet red-polished floor, security gate to the garden. Friday.
lines: The roof has no gutter on that side and tonight it is a waterfall.
Rain coming off the roof in one solid sheet: the stoep has a curtain tonight.
Everything past the gate is weather; everything inside it is fine.

images.why: round-1 lines retired by the doctrine redo
images.seen: Lightning glowing behind heavy cloud over a small-town street at night, one streetlight on, a white car safe under its carport behind the gate. Thursday.
lines: The whole sky went mauve for a second and the street pretended not to notice.
One streetlight versus the entire electrical budget of that cloud.
That flash reached town before its thunder; the gap is closing though.
